newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SENTRACHEM IN $75 MLN HERBICIDE INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: SENTRACHEM IN $75 MLN HERBICIDE INVESTMENT.

text.p: South African chemicals firm Sentrachem Ltd said on Wednesday it would invest $75 million over the next four years in the production of top-selling herbicide glyphosate.

Sentrachem is to enter the market through Sanachem, its South African manufacturer and marketer of generic crop protection chemicals, and U.S.-based Hampshire Chemical Corporation which it acquired in September last year.
Managing director John Job said the group plans to build two modular production units in South Africa with a total capacity of 5,000 tonnes. The first of these is set to come on stream next year.
A third plant of up to 20,000 tonnes capacity will be built at Hampshire Chemical's site in Texas by the year 2000.
Job said the move would have a significant impact on group earnings in years to come, with early benefits being seen in the 1997 financial year.
The world market for glyphosate -- a biodegradable, systemic herbicide -- is about 70,000 tonnes and growing by 15 percent a year.
